text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the position-dependent spinning sensation is a key clue. Given your age and history of hearing loss, have you noticed any sudden, severe hearing loss or tinnitus (ringing in the ears) in the last few days? speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of position-dependent vertigo in a 70-year-old woman with a history of presbycusis is highly specific for BPPV. No further testing or questions are required to confirm this diagnosis; the Dix-Hallpike maneuver would typically be the next step for definitive confirmation and treatment in a clinical setting.
